title: Relative search in the embedding viewer

claims.text: The embedding viewer has relative search: with a search active, the view can be measured from the search, so that one axis on screen is the search direction, a point's position along it is its similarity to the search, and the remaining axes keep tumbling

honesty_conditions.text: The reference page on the real Wikipedia set shows the behaviour the announcement describes, and the owner has opened it and agrees it is the intended behaviour.

claims.text: People who search an embedding set in the viewer and want to read how every point relates to the search, not only which few points were returned; and hosts who embed the viewer and already supply a search.

honesty_conditions.text: The search guide explains the relative view to both readers and a host can turn it on through the documented API without reading the source.

claims.instruction: Check docs/guides/search.md names both readers in its relative-search section.

claims.text: A search lights its results and swings or fits the view to them, but the middle of the screen is an average (of the set in Tumble, of the results in Focus) and no axis has a meaning. Position on screen cannot be read as similarity to the search, and the origin is not shown anywhere.

honesty_conditions.text: The built viewer still passes every existing Tumble, Focus and search test with relative off, with no change to any existing frame (bit-identical to 0.12.1 for the same data, seed and time).

claims.instruction: Verify against js/src/40-mode-tumble.js (centre is st.mean) and js/src/26-search-sets.js finish() (centre is the mean of the results' centres).

claims.text: With relative on and at least one search, the first search's direction is the vertical axis. A point's height is its vector measured along that direction, which is cosine similarity when the vectors have length one. A ruler with ticks is drawn along the axis from the origin, each named result is joined to the height it is read at, and the other axes tour the strongest directions of the set after the search direction is removed. Turning relative off, or removing the last search, returns to the plain view.

honesty_conditions.text: The built viewer and the reference page agree, for the same search on the Wikipedia demo set, on which axis is pinned and on every named result's height to 2 decimal places.

claims.instruction: Compare side by side with docs/specs/reference/tumbler-relative-search.html on the Wikipedia demo set with the same search.

claims.text: Real sets sit in a narrow cone (Wikipedia demo set: mean vector 0.79 from the origin, cosines to one article between 0.52 and 0.84). A view centred on the average hides that and gives position no meaning for a search. Pinning one axis to the search makes one coordinate on screen exact and readable for all points at once.

honesty_conditions.text: The cone figures (mean length 0.79, cosine range 0.52 to 0.84) are reproduced by a script in the repository and recorded in docs/evidence, and a second real set of a different model is measured before the claim is written as general.

claims.instruction: The numbers are in scope finding s4; restate them in docs/evidence when the build measures them again.

claims.text: Relative search changes only the frame, the centre, the zoom and what is drawn over the picture. It adds no new kind of projection, changes no vector, changes nothing in the data contract and sends nothing anywhere. It is a way of viewing existing searches (typed words, a host embed callback, or the helper route), not a new way of searching.

honesty_conditions.text: A network log in the browser tests shows no request made by turning relative on, and the data contract tests pass unchanged.

claims.instruction: The diff must not touch docs/data-contract.md, js/src/20-contract.js or embeddings_tumbler/_embed_route.py.

claims.text: No rescaling of vectors to unit length for display. When vectors are not of length one the axis is still exact and is labelled as length along the search direction, not as cosine.
No UMAP, t-SNE or other non-linear layout, and no distance-preserving layout around the search.

The pinned axis is exact: for every point, its coordinate along the pinned frame row equals the dot product of its vector with the unit search direction, to float32 accuracy, at every moment of the tour.

scope_entries.finding: Tumble's frame is a closed-form tour inside the 8 strongest principal directions of the centred set; its centre is the set's mean (centreTau glide). Nothing in it is measured from the origin or from a search. The tour takes any orthonormal basis and any number of directions of at least three, so a tour restricted to directions orthogonal to a search needs a tour of two rows or one row, which makeTour does not offer today (it always returns three rows).

The renderer already accepts any centre vector and any three orthonormal frame rows, and has a fog setting that dims by true full-dimension distance from the centre. It draws with a fixed perspective; the reference draws the relative view almost flat so that heights read true. There is no ruler, tick, ring or origin marker in the renderer or the overlay today.

Search today changes the view in two ways: Tumble swings its frame toward the searched points and releases back to the tour; Focus fits a facing frame to queries and results and centres on the mean of the results. Neither pins an axis to a query direction and neither centres on the query or the origin. Up to four searches (letters A to D) are supported.

All 999 vectors have length 1 (0.99999997 to 1.00000002). The mean vector has length 0.79, so the set sits in a narrow cone far from the origin. Cosine to a single article ranges about 0.52 to 0.84 over the whole set (median about 0.62). After removing a search direction, the 8 strongest remaining directions hold 18 percent of the remaining variance, and the cloud's centre sits up to about 0.18 off the search axis in those directions (per-direction spread about 0.07 to 0.14). The plain tour's 8 directions also hold 18 percent.

The contract does not require unit-length vectors and the viewer does not assume them; the spec fixes linear projections only, reproducible views from a seed, and that every view states it is a shadow. Rescaling each vector to unit length before drawing would not be a linear projection of the data as supplied.

A working reference page on the real Wikipedia set was built first. It shows: search A pinned to the vertical axis with a ticked ruler from the origin; results joined by stems to the height they are read at; two free axes touring 8 directions orthogonal to the search; a second search B drawn as a second ruler in the plane it shares with A (horizontal axis is what B adds beyond A) with only depth touring; a Show the origin control; a Plain view for comparison in which the origin marker reports its true and its visible distance. A search there is an article in the set or the mean of matched titles, because the page has no embedding model.

The reranker is a host callback rerank(query, candidates) returning scores and a model id; the core file never fetches. The pool is the 50 nearest named points by default and the best 20 are kept; each hit records its embedding rank, new rank, places moved and score. viewer serve --embed --rerank-model offers Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B through the gateway. An Artifact page cannot call it, so the reference page reads scores made ahead of time by scripts/build_reference_rerank.py (one search per article, the article's text against its 50 nearest others).
